{"name": "charge-review", "steps": "Goal: decide from console evidence and current policy what Support may do about a charge, do it with approval, and tell the developer.

1. Gather. If the developer has not given them, call `ask_developer` once for the org (or account id), the invoice id or month, and the lines/amounts in question; add request ids if they say specific requests were mis-billed.
2. Read, in one round: `account_overview` (org or account id) and `search_knowledge` for the policy on this kind of request (e.g. "duplicate charge credit Support limit", "refund request billed in error", "goodwill credit request", "SLA credit request contract"). Then `invoice_details` for the invoice. If the developer gave only a month, pick the invoice whose period covers it.
3. Check the billing channel first. If the account is billed by a marketplace or reseller, Support does not credit or dispute that invoice: find the policy for that channel and tell the developer who handles it.
4. Classify with console evidence only:
   - Duplicate: `console_confirmed_duplicates` lists the lines (same request ids on the same invoice). Same description or amount alone is not a duplicate; lines in `lookalike_lines` bill different requests and are separate charges: explain that with the request ids and times, then follow the policy row for a duplicate the console does not confirm.
   - Already credited: the line shows `credited_cents` or a credit note exists; say so, don't credit again.
   - Correct charge the developer wants removed or reduced (goodwill, waiver, SLA/service credit, exception, retries): Support explains why it is billed and routes the request per policy; it issues nothing.
   - Wrong rate, quantity or unexplained amount: route per policy with the evidence.
5. For a confirmed duplicate, find Support's current per-line limit in the retrieved policy (check it is the authoritative, current source; drafts and proposals don't count). If the duplicated line is within the limit: `confirm_with_developer` ("credit note of $X on line L of invoice I, reason duplicate"), then `issue_credit_note` for the full line amount on that one line with reason `duplicate`, citing `policy_source` and `policy_limit`. If over the limit: don't credit; confirm, `open_dispute` on the duplicated line (reason `duplicate_charge`, with its request ids), then `escalate_case` to the team policy names with the dispute id.
6. Routing without a write: load the `billing-handoff` skill.
7. Reply: what the console shows (lines, request ids, amounts), what you did (credit note id and amount, or dispute/case and team), and what happens next. Don't promise outcomes, refund timing or amounts the policy doesn't state."}

{"name": "billing-handoff", "steps": "1. Decide whether a case is needed. Search the routing policy (`search_knowledge`, e.g. "billing case routing <topic>"). If a current page explains what the developer sees, or they only asked a question (how something is billed, what their contract says, typical amounts), answer it and stop: no case. Open a case only when they ask for something Support can't do in the conversation, or report a problem the pages don't explain.
2. Pick the owning team from the current routing passage for this exact situation. Watch for the distinguishing condition in each row: billing channel (direct vs marketplace/reseller), plan (self-serve vs contract), whether the charge is an error or correct, whether the console confirms the problem. If the developer claims something the console doesn't show (e.g. a contract), follow the policy row for that.
3. Collect the intake that row lists. Use what the developer already wrote and the console; call `ask_developer` once for the rest (e.g. invoice_id, line_items, request_ids, time_of_issue + timezone, error_code, checks_done, contract). If they don't have something, proceed and record it as missing.
4. Answer everything you can first: escalation closes the console for the rest of the conversation.
5. `confirm_with_developer`: "I'll hand this to <team> with <key facts>." If they decline, don't escalate; tell them how to come back.
6. `escalate_case` once: team, a summary (what they asked, what the console shows, what policy says, what you already did), details (account_id, invoice_id, line_ids, request_ids, amounts, UTC window, error code, plan/contract, missing items, policy source ids), and the dispute id if any.
7. Tell the developer the team that has it, the case id, what that team does next per policy, and that you can't promise an outcome, amount or date."}

| Meter discrepancy the related pages don't explain: request IDs whose billed tokens still don't match after the tokenizer, payload and retry rules are applied | Billing Engineering | Billing Eng checks meter correctness and hands any correction to Billing Ops |"}, {"source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/support-console-billing-credits-and-disputes", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Support Console: Duplicate-Charge Credits and Billing Disputes", "status": "published", "updated": "2026-02-05", "text": "meta: author=Dev Patel; owner_team=customer-success; labels=billing, credits, disputes, support-console, support-process; created_at=2026-01-27
[body]
## Purpose
The support console can look up a customer's billing account, issue a credit note against invoice lines, and open a billing dispute. This page defines when Support uses each one. It amends the billing routing page for duplicate charges only; everything else on that page still applies.
## Look up the account first
- Look up the customer's billing account in the console before you quote an amount, a plan, an invoice line, or whether a charge is a duplicate. You can find the account by its account id or by the customer's org name; ask for one of them if the customer hasn't given either.
- Quote amounts as the console shows them. Don't restate a figure the customer gives you as fact."}, {"source": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "updated": "2026-02-03", "text": "| Promotional or campaign credits | Growth marketing | Within the campaign budget FP&A approved |
| Partner program funds (MDF) | Partnerships | Per the partner agreement; never applied to invoices |
| Write-off of an uncollectible balance | Controller | Up to $10,000; above that, the CFO |
| Re-issued invoice (address, PO number, tax ID) | Billing Ops | No limit; no change to amounts |
## Evidence each adjustment needs
- **Duplicate-charge credit**: the invoice number, both line IDs and the request IDs they bill. The console confirms the duplicate; a matching description or amount alone is not evidence.
- **Billing-error correction**: the line, the expected rate or quantity and where it comes from (price book, order form).
- **Goodwill and SLA credits**: the customer's ask, the amount if given, and the reason. The account team adds contract references for SLA claims.
- **Write-offs**: collections history and the Controller's note."}, {"source": "google_drive/shared_drives/finance/billing-adjustments-approval-matrix", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Billing Adjustments Approval Matrix", "status": "final", "updated": "2026-02-03", "text": "- **Goodwill**: any reduction of a correct charge, for any reason.
## Approval matrix
| Adjustment | Who issues it | Limit and approver |
|---|---|---|
| Duplicate-charge credit (console-confirmed duplicate line on a direct invoice) | Support, from the support console | Up to $500 per duplicated line. Over that, Support opens a dispute and Billing Ops takes it |
| Billing-error correction other than a duplicate (wrong rate, quantity or product) | Billing Ops | Up to $2,000 per invoice; above that, the Controller |
| Refund of a paid invoice line after an approved adjustment | Billing Ops | Up to $5,000; above that, the Controller |
| Goodwill credit, waiver, or exception to a billing rule | Finance (FP&A) | Any amount, decided in FP&A's review. Support and Billing Ops route these requests and never issue them |
| SLA credit on a self-serve account | Finance (FP&A) | Self-serve plans carry no SLA. FP&A reviews any request as goodwill |
| SLA credit under a signed contract | Account team files the claim; Finance approves | Per the contract's SLA terms. No amount is promised before Finance's review |"}, {"source": "gmail/jasmine_liu/20260518-marketplace-cross-cloud-duplicate-metering-and-uk-vat-reclass", "kind": "case record or discussion", "title": "Email: Discrepancy on May marketplace invoice - duplicate metering lines & VAT routing", "status": "n/a", "updated": "2026-05-20", "text": "Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discrepancy on May invoice - duplicate marketplace lines (AWS + GCP)
Hi Jasmine,
We're reviewing our May charges and flagged a set of duplicate marketplace line items that appear to have been billed through both AWS Marketplace and GCP Marketplace for the same usage window and meter IDs. Attached: BrightLane_Invoice_May2026.pdf and a raw metering_export_may.csv from our billing system with the offending meter IDs highlighted.
Key example: Meter ID 3837-ALPHA appears on both the AWS line (line 42) and the GCP line (line 129) with identical usage units and timestamp ranges. Total potential overcharge ≈ $7,120.

- Proposed remediation: credit memo or offset path (which marketplace will issue the credit)
- VAT handling: We're a UK entity and need to confirm if VAT was applied on both legs — we cannot accept duplicate VAT."}, {"source": "confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/duplicate-charges-and-refunds-help-2025", "kind": "policy/procedure page", "title": "Help Center: Duplicate Charges and Refunds (archived)", "status": "published (archived)", "updated": "2026-01-21", "text": "meta: author=Dev Patel; owner_team=customer-success; created_at=2025-06-10; labels=help-center, billing, refunds, archived

Recommendation:
1) Issue customer-facing credit of $7,120 plus a VAT credit memo of $1,424.
2) Route the gross credit via AWS Marketplace offset where possible for the AWS-billed lines (faster settlement), and request a refund request to Google for the GCP line (GCP refunds take longer).
